content.text:
If you mean **free SiriusXM / satellite radio in your car**, your legal options are:

1. **SiriusXM Free Access** — SiriusXM has a free streaming tier with a limited channel lineup. ([siriusxm.com](https://www.siriusxm.com/plans/free-access?utm_source=openai))  
2. **SiriusXM free trial** — SiriusXM offers free trials; some require registration and may renew unless canceled before the renewal date. ([siriusxm.com](https://www.siriusxm.com/free-trial?utm_source=openai))  
3. **Used-car / pre-owned trial** — many vehicles with a factory SiriusXM radio may qualify for a **3-month trial**, sometimes with no credit card depending on the offer. ([swaggrabber.com](https://swaggrabber.com/siriusxm-radio-free-trial/?utm_source=openai))  
4. **Listen Free Events** — SiriusXM periodically turns on inactive car radios for a short free preview. The most recent widely reported 2026 event was **May 21–June 1, 2026**, so it has already ended as of today, **June 8, 2026**. ([seniordaily.com](https://www.seniordaily.com/siriusxm-free-listen-preview/?utm_source=openai))  

If you meant **truly free satellite signals**, SiriusXM is not normally free-to-air; it’s a subscription satellite radio service. For free audio, you may be better off with **AM/FM radio, HD Radio, internet radio apps, podcasts, or free streaming tiers**.
